name: Intercom
verdict: Self-serve to build, but Intercom must review every public app before any customer can install, even unlisted ones. Review takes up to 7 business days; budget 1-3 weeks with the video and forms.
needGuide: Yes — prepare the OAuth install, features and uninstall video plus the App Partner Program form before you submit.

auth.detail: Authorization code flow with client_secret and a state parameter (PKCE not documented). Authorization endpoint is regional (US/EU/AU); code exchanged at https://api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token for a Bearer access token. Token lifetime and refresh not covered in the fetched docs (tokens likely non-expiring).

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 weeks incl. video, forms and review (up to 7 business days)

approval.gate: Mandatory Intercom review for any public app (listed or unlisted) before customers can install. Review takes up to 7 business days. Submit an app description, App Partner Program form, and an end-to-end video of OAuth install, features and uninstall. App Store listing is optional after approval.

scopes.why: Scopes are picked in the Developer Hub; reviewers compare them with the app's features and may ask you to trim and resubmit.
scopes.summary: Pick scopes in Developer Hub; reviewers compare them to actual functionality and may ask you to trim and resubmit. Webhook topics are tied to scopes. Canvas Kit apps get some scopes automatically.

cost: Free (development workspaces are free); reviewer needs test credentials if the app needs a paid plan
prerequisites: Account and owner: An Intercom teammate account that can open Developer Hub; public apps must be built in a separate free development workspace.
Where you register: Developer Hub → Your apps → New App → Configure → Authentication → tick Use OAuth; add HTTPS redirect URLs and scopes
Cost: Free (development workspaces are free); reviewer needs test credentials if the app needs a paid plan

registerAt.path: Developer Hub → Your apps → New App → Configure → Authentication → tick Use OAuth; add HTTPS redirect URLs and scopes

steps.do: Create a free development workspace, then Developer Hub → New App
Authentication page: tick Use OAuth, add HTTPS redirect URLs (staging + production), choose minimal scopes
Implement authorize redirect with random state; POST code, client_id, client_secret to /auth/eagle/token
Verify with GET /me and test install and uninstall in the dev workspace
Complete App Listing and App Partner Program form in Test and publish
Record video showing OAuth install with full client_id and state visible, all features, and uninstall
Submit for Review and answer feedback in the Messenger conversation

roles.team: An Intercom teammate account that can open Developer Hub; public apps must be built in a separate free development workspace.
roles.console: None documented for app collaborators; creators/submitters receive review notifications.
roles.customer: A workspace teammate who installs the app via OAuth consent. Specific permission level not documented in fetched pages (likely admin-level).

testing: Free development workspaces: US-only, capped at 20 users/leads, no outbound email or push, cannot be converted to production.
During review the app stays private to your team.

blockers.fix: Plan the video and forms up front.
Map each scope to a visible feature.
Dev workspaces are US-only, so use regional auth endpoints and test carefully.

blockers.problem: Approved apps need re-approval for changes
blockers.fix: Keep a private staging app alongside the public one.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth code and regional endpoint handling, draft listing copy, scope justifications and video script, and run test API calls.
automation.humanMust: Create the workspace/app in the console, record the demo video, submit the review, communicate via the Intercom Messenger, and accept partner terms.

uncertain: Token expiry/refresh behavior; customer-side permission needed to install; App Store guideline details (guidelines and listing pages were not fetched).
